in_context.text: This verse sits in a section on prayer and conduct in worship (2:1-15). Paul has just told men to pray without anger (2:8) and women to dress modestly and be known for good works (2:9-10). Here he says how women should learn, and the next verses restrict women from teaching or taking authority over a man (2:12-14).

speaker.text: Paul the apostle, who names himself at the start of the letter. Many critical scholars think a follower wrote in Paul's name, while others defend Paul's authorship.

audience.text: Timothy, Paul's younger co-worker, whom Paul had left to lead the church at Ephesus.

affected.text: Women in the church's gatherings for prayer and worship.

what.text: Paul instructs that a woman should learn, doing so in quietness and with full submission. The Greek word for silence can also mean quietness, and the verb is a command to learn.

events.text: The instruction concerns the ongoing life of the church at Ephesus while Timothy led it. The church there was facing false teaching from within.

written.text: Traditional view: about AD 62-64, between Paul's two Roman imprisonments. Scholarly view: many critical scholars date it around AD 80-110.

where.text: The letter was sent to Ephesus, a wealthy port and capital of the Roman province of Asia, known for its temple of Artemis. Where Paul wrote from is not stated, possibly Macedonia.

purpose.text: Paul is guiding how believers should behave in worship and in the household of God. This verse sets the manner in which women are to learn in the gathered church.

big_picture.text: The chapter starts with God wanting all people to be saved and come to know the truth (2:4). Learning the truth is the goal, and this verse includes women as learners. Paul grounds the following restrictions in the order of creation and Eve's deception (2:13-14).

for_readers.text: Readers should read this verse together with 2:12-15 and with similar passages such as 1 Corinthians 14:34-35. The letter links right belief with right behavior in the church.

misuse.popular_reading: Quoted alone as a blanket rule that women must never speak, anywhere.

in_context_reading.text: The setting is the church's gatherings for prayer and worship. The verse also commands that women learn. Its key word can mean quietness, not only total silence.

why_it_matters.text: The verb is a command: women are to learn. The verse is about how women take part as learners, not about keeping them out.
The word means quietness, stillness, or silence. It is used for quiet living in 2 Thessalonians 3:12, so it may describe a calm, attentive manner rather than total silence.
The word means submission or subjection. It appears again in 1 Timothy 3:4. This verse does not say whom the submission is directed to.

takeaway.text: Paul tells women in the Ephesian church to learn, in quietness and submission, within the church's worship. Read it with its whole paragraph, and alongside Paul's charge that older women be "teachers of good things" to younger women (Titus 2:3-5).
